when: before 3:00
asks: how do I play the first waves
should I push or hold at the start
push first wave or nah
what do I do with the wave level one
say: Push the first wave to hit level two first and crash it, or hold it even if their champion beats yours at level one.
more: Level two first gives you one trade with an extra ability. Crashing after it makes the wave bounce back toward your tower, the safe place to be when junglers finish their first clear.
Holding it even gives up that trade but keeps you out of their half, so an early gank has only a short chase.
check: Who is winning the level one exchange, and which way the wave is drifting.
breaks: If they out-trade you while you push, stop hitting the wave and last-hit only; pushed up with low health is a gank waiting to happen.

when: between 2:45 and 4:15
asks: is it safe to shove now
am I gonna get ganked if I push
wave's pushing to them, is that ok
should I be pushed up right now
say: Junglers finish first clears about now, so crash the wave fully and step back, or thin it and hold near your side.
more: Both river crabs spawn at 2:55 and a full clear ends around level four, so the minutes after three are when a jungler first shows up top.
A wave that reaches their tower bounces back to you. A wave stuck halfway into their side is the worst spot: a long run home and nothing gained.
check: Whether the wave can actually reach their tower before you have to leave, and whether river is warded.
breaks: If you cannot finish the crash, stop pushing and let it come back; half a push is worse than none.

when: enemy top is dead
asks: he's dead what do I do with the wave
I killed him, push or back
enemy top's dead now what
should I shove after the kill
say: Shove the whole wave into their tower so it dies there, then recall on the crash, or stay for plates if you're healthy.
more: The kill only pays if they also lose minions. A wave that dies to their tower is gold and experience they never get; a wave left in the middle waits for them.
Recall as it crashes and you come back with items to a wave walking toward you, so the lead is an item as well as a kill.
check: How big the wave is, your health, and whether their jungler could arrive before the wave crashes.
breaks: If you're too low to finish the shove safely, recall at once and take the smaller gain; dying to the jungler hands the kill back.
basis: pro:Kills are not a lead if the farm went the other way

when: you died in the last minute
asks: I just died, how do I get back in lane
coming back to lane what do I do with the wave
wave's at my tower after dying
lost a wave, how do I fix it
say: Catch the wave at your tower and last-hit only so it stays on your side, or shove it out if they're freezing it.
more: After a death the wave usually comes to you. Last-hitting only keeps it near your tower, where you get farm back and their jungler has a long way to chase.
If instead they hold it just outside your tower range, you must push hard, because a held wave denies you every minion.
check: Where the wave sits when you arrive, and whether the enemy top recalled or stayed.
breaks: If they stayed with a big wave and you are still low on items, do not walk into it; wait at the tower and let it crash.

when: you lead the enemy top in level or CS and you have a kill on them
asks: I'm ahead, how do I keep him down
should I freeze
how do I deny him farm
push or freeze when winning
say: Hold the wave just outside your tower and zone them off it, or crash it and take plates if their jungler's shown elsewhere.
more: A held wave makes them choose between losing minions and walking far up a long lane next to a stronger champion. That grows a small lead without any risk.
Plates are the other way to cash in: more gold now, but the wave resets and they get to farm again.
check: Whether the enemy wave is slightly bigger than yours, which is what keeps a freeze in place, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If your own jungler wants to dive, or an objective is close, a freeze is the wrong shape; push it in instead.

when: your CS is falling behind the enemy top's and their items have not changed
asks: he's freezing on me what do I do
how do I break a freeze
I can't get to the wave
he's zoning me off cs
say: If they're holding the wave by their tower, ask your jungler to help shove it in, or recall now and return with items.
more: A freeze only ends when the wave reaches their tower. Alone and behind you usually can't force that; a second body or a bigger wave does it.
Recalling while frozen out costs less than it feels: you were not getting those minions anyway, and you come back with health and a component.
check: Where the wave really sits, whether they are still in lane, and whether your jungler is near enough to come.
breaks: If the wave is actually moving toward you, it isn't a freeze; wait for it at your tower instead of recalling.

when: your team just killed a dragon, or your jungler just took part in a kill on their bot laner or support
asks: my jungler's bot, how do I play
no help top what do I do with wave
I'm weak side right
jungler never comes top
say: Your help is bot side, so hold the wave near your tower and skip even trades, or shove only if their jungler shows bot too.
more: When your team plays the other half of the map, the enemy jungler's best move is your lane. Your job for that minute is to give nothing back.
It costs a few minions and maybe a plate. It sets up the next rotation, when you arrive alive and they got nothing for losing bot side.
check: Where your jungler and mid are right now, and whether the enemy jungler has been seen.
breaks: If their jungler is confirmed on the far side as well, the lane is a plain one against one and you can play it normally.
basis: pro:The lane without help gives nothing

when: between 7:00 and 8:00
asks: grubs are coming what do I do top
how do I set up for grubs
should I push before grubs
wave before grubs
say: Grubs come at eight, so start a slow push now and crash it just before, or keep it at your tower if you're giving them.
more: Grubs are a single window from 8:00 and never come back. The laner whose wave is already under the enemy tower walks to the pit first.
The other laner either loses a big wave to the tower or shows up late and alone. If your team is giving grubs, minions and plates are your payment.
check: Whether your jungler is actually pathing to grubs, and which top laner can win the fight in river.
breaks: If you lose the one against one, pushing just walks you into a fight you lose; hold the wave and concede.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: enemy jungler is dead
asks: their jungler's dead can I push
jungler died should I go up
is it safe to hit tower now
what do I do while their jungler's dead
say: Their jungler's dead, so push past the middle and hit the tower while it's safe, or ward deep and back off before he's up.
more: Most top lane deaths need a second enemy. While the respawn timer runs, the only threats are the top laner and a roaming mid.
A deep ward placed now keeps paying after he respawns: you see his next path and know when to pull the wave back.
check: His respawn timer, and whether their mid laner is missing from lane.
breaks: If the enemy top beats you alone, a dead jungler changes nothing; keep the wave where you were holding it.

when: you are a ranged champion and the enemy top is melee
asks: I'm ranged how do I manage the wave
should I keep pushing as ranged
how do I bully with the wave
wave as ranged top
say: Keep the wave pushing gently and hit them when they walk up to last-hit, or hold it mid-lane if you haven't seen their jungler.
more: Your attacks push the wave whether you want it or not, so plan for it: a wave near their tower lets you harass every last-hit.
The price is a long lane behind you. Ranged tops lose leads to one gank, so the ward and the jungler sighting matter more than the poke.
check: River and tri-brush vision, and whether their dash or engage is available.
breaks: If their jungler is unseen and you have no escape, last-hit only and let the wave sit in the middle.

when: enemy top is a ranged champion and you are melee
asks: he's ranged how do I farm
can't cs against ranged
where do I want the wave against ranged
ranged top keeps pushing me in
say: Let them push to you and last-hit just outside tower range, where a gank has a long chase, or give the minions you can't reach.
more: A ranged champion pushes naturally. Near your tower they must stand far from safety to keep poking, which is the one thing a melee champion and a jungler can punish.
Minions you give up early come back later; health you lose to poke does not come back without a recall.
check: Whether the wave is reaching your tower or stopping just short of it.
breaks: If they crash it fully and walk away to roam or recall, shove back at once rather than waiting.

when: enemy jungler is alive and has not appeared in a kill or objective event for two minutes
asks: where's their jungler
is it safe to push top
haven't seen jungler should I back up
can I push or is he coming
say: Nobody's seen their jungler, so pull the wave back to your side and give a couple of minions, or push only with river warded.
more: A jungler who isn't where his route should put him is information in itself. Treat him as close until someone actually sees him.
Your own jungler being nearby says nothing about theirs. Backing off costs two or three minions; guessing wrong costs a wave, a death and often plates.
check: When and where he was last seen, and whether you have a ward on the path into your lane.
breaks: Once he shows anywhere else on the map, the caution ends and you can step up again.
basis: pro:A jungler missing from where he should be is information

when: enemy top just took part in a kill on someone other than you
asks: he roamed what do I do
enemy top left lane
top's missing should I follow
he teleported bot now what
say: They left lane, so shove and take plates while they're gone, or follow with Teleport if that fight is still going.
more: You can rarely beat a roam by walking after it. Taking the wave and tower gold they abandoned is a payment that starts immediately.
Following is right only when the fight is still undecided and you arrive in time to change it; arriving after it ends loses both.
check: Whether you have Teleport ready, whether the fight elsewhere is over, and how far the wave is from their tower.
breaks: If their jungler is also unaccounted for and you are low, take the wave and stop short of the tower.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

asks: how do I slow push
how do I set up a big wave
how do I stack a wave
want to dive him how do I set the wave
say: Kill only their back minions so your wave builds, then crash it big for a recall or a dive, or just fast-shove if time's short.
more: Leaving their front minions alive lets your next wave join the first. Two waves arriving together are hard to clear and hold tower aggro for a long time.
A big crash buys a clean recall, a dive with your jungler or a walk to river. A fast shove gets there sooner with less behind it.
check: Whether the enemy can simply clear the stacked wave with abilities, and whether you can survive a trade while it builds.
breaks: If they fight you inside your building wave and win, stop; the plan needs you healthy when it arrives.

asks: big wave coming at me what do I do
huge wave pushing into me
should I meet the wave or wait
wave's bouncing back
say: Let a big wave come all the way and farm it at your tower, or meet it early only if you're healthy and win the trade.
more: Walking out to meet a large enemy wave means fighting with all of their minions hitting you. At the tower the minions are busy and the trade flips.
Once it is cleared, the wave pushes back out on its own and you get a free step forward.
check: How many minions are in it, and whether their jungler could be behind it for a dive.
breaks: If you are low and their jungler is unseen, a big wave is a dive setup; step behind the tower or give it.

asks: should I freeze as Nasus
how do I stack safely
where do I want the wave as Nasus
Nasus wave
say: Hold the wave by your tower and last-hit with Siphoning Strike, since it grows with each kill, or shove and recall if you're getting chunked.
more: Every minion finished with Siphoning Strike makes the next one hit harder for the rest of the game, so a quiet wave near your tower is your best lane.
Wither is your answer to being run at. It slows their movement and attacks, which is usually enough to get back to the tower.
check: Whether they are letting you last-hit or zoning you off the wave.
breaks: If you are being denied every minion, stop standing in it; give the wave, recall and ask for jungle help.

when: your top outer tower has fallen
asks: my tower's gone where do I farm
lost outer tower how do I play top
can I still farm top
where do I catch the wave now
say: With your outer tower gone, catch the wave near your inner tower and don't push past halfway alone, or group if it's already pushed out.
more: The lane is now much longer on your side. Anything past the halfway point is a place where two or three enemies can cut you off.
Farming by the inner tower still gets you every wave. It is slower, but it is gold with an exit.
check: How many enemies are visible on the map before you step past the old tower.
breaks: If most of their team shows on the far side, you can push further for a short while; leave when they disappear.

when: before 2:00 and both top laners are level 1
asks: should I fight level one
can I trade at the start
do I go for him level one
level one fight or no
say: Fight level one only if your champion wins it and you're standing in your own minions, or just give the first few last-hits.
more: At level one the minions do a large share of the damage. Whoever fights inside the other side's wave usually loses, whatever the champions are.
Giving two or three last-hits to stay healthy costs little. Losing half your health before level two costs the next several waves.
check: Which first ability each of you took, and whose minions you would be standing in.
breaks: If they start walking through your minions to reach you, turn and fight; your wave is now on your side.

when: you are level 2 and the enemy top is level 1
asks: I hit two first do I go
level two should I trade
got level two now what
do I fight now
say: You're level two first, so trade now with both abilities before they catch up, or zone them off the minions if they back away.
more: For a few seconds you have two abilities against one. Early on a level is worth more than a small gold or farm difference.
If they retreat instead, standing between them and the wave delays their own level two, and the window stays open longer.
check: How many of their minions are still alive to hit you during the trade.
breaks: If the trade would happen deep in a full enemy wave, zone instead of committing.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: the enemy top is level 2 and you are level 1
asks: he got level two first
he's level two what do I do
should I back off he leveled
can I still trade
say: They hit two first, so step back behind your minions until you level, or give one last-hit rather than take the trade.
more: Their window lasts only until your next few minions die. Standing a little further back for that moment is all it takes to close it.
After you level, the lane is even again and nothing was lost except perhaps one minion.
check: How close you are to your own level two.
breaks: If they stay back and do not use the lead, keep last-hitting as normal.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: you are level 6 and the enemy top is level 5
asks: I'm six he's not do I go in
I have ult should I all in
level six first what now
can I kill him now
say: You have your ultimate and they don't, so look for the all-in this wave, or hold it and call your jungler for a sure kill.
more: This is usually the largest gap the lane ever has, and it closes as soon as they finish a wave or two.
A kill here means a shoved wave, a recall and an item lead going into the grub window.
check: Their health, their Flash, and whether a big enemy wave would fight with them.
breaks: If they hug the tower at full health, do not dive alone; shove the wave so they stay under it and lose farm instead.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: the enemy top is level 6 and you are level 5
asks: he's six and I'm not
he got ult first what do I do
should I respect his six
he's level six can I still fight
say: They're six first, so stay near your tower until you level, or trade only if you saw their ultimate used.
more: A level and an ultimate together are too much to trade into. The gap lasts only until you finish your own level.
If the wave is in a bad spot, giving a few minions is the cheap way through it.
check: How far you are from level six, and how much health you have.
breaks: If their ultimate was just spent on something else, the levels are close enough to fight normally.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: enemy top is a ranged champion and you are melee
asks: how do I trade against ranged
he pokes me every time I walk up
when do I go in on ranged
can't get close to him
say: Wait in brush and go in when their escape or slow is used, or just take last-hits and skip trading altogether.
more: Ranged champions win by hitting you for free. Brush hides your approach and drops their minions off you, so use it to shorten the walk.
Their one defensive tool is usually a dash, a slow or a blind. Once it is used you have several seconds where you win.
check: Whether their escape ability was just used, and how big their wave is.
breaks: If you reach them at half health, the trade is already lost; reset and try again from full.

when: you are a ranged champion and the enemy top is melee
asks: how do I poke without dying
when do I auto him
how do I trade as ranged top
he keeps jumping on me
say: Poke when they step up for a last-hit, then walk back out of their dash range, or stop poking if the wave's dragging you forward.
more: They must come forward to last-hit, and that moment is your free hit. Hitting them at other times pulls their minions onto you.
Every attack on them also pushes you up the lane. Count how far you are from your tower, not only how low they are.
check: Whether their gap closer is available and how far you are from safety.
breaks: If they have reached level six or bought boots and can now reach you, play further back and poke less often.

when: you are a tank and the enemy top is a fighter
asks: how do I trade as a tank
bruiser keeps beating me in trades
can I fight him as tank
tank into fighter trading
say: Trade short: one ability, then walk out before their damage ramps, or skip trades and farm until your first defensive item.
more: Fighters win long exchanges and tanks win brief ones. One ability and out leaves them with nothing to hit.
Your lane goal is to arrive at the first big fights healthy and even in farm. A drawn lane is a win for the tank.
check: Whether their main damage ability is ready, and whether you can leave after your own.
breaks: If they are low and your jungler is here, commit fully; a tank with help does not need to trade short.

when: enemy top is a tank with no completed item
asks: how do I punish a tank early
can I fight the tank
tank's just farming what do I do
how do I trade into a tank
say: Take long trades now, before their first defensive item, or shove and take plates if they just sit under tower.
more: This is when a tank is weakest in lane. Each trade should cost them health they cannot easily get back.
If they refuse to fight, tower plates are how the lead is taken. The lane becomes gold for you rather than kills.
check: Whether they have bought armor or magic resist yet, and where their jungler is.
breaks: If they have a defensive item and you have nothing finished, long trades stop working; switch to pushing.

when: your health is below half
asks: I'm low can I still trade
should I keep fighting
I'm half health what do I do
do I back or stay
say: You're low, so stop trading and last-hit from as far back as you can, or recall on the next push if they can run you down.
more: Below half, one more trade puts you in kill range of the laner and in dive range of their jungler.
A recall now loses part of a wave. Staying and dying loses the wave, the gold and usually plates as well.
check: Their health compared with yours, and whether they have the tools to run you down.
breaks: If they are even lower and their abilities were just used, one decisive trade can still be right.

asks: why do I lose every trade
minions are killing me
I keep losing trades with more health
why did I lose that
say: Trade when your wave's bigger, since their minions hit you whenever you hit them, or step into brush to shake them off.
more: Attacking an enemy champion turns every nearby enemy minion onto you. Early on a full wave does as much damage as an ability.
Count minions before you go. If theirs outnumber yours, either wait a few seconds or trade next to the brush.
check: How many minions each side has at the moment you want to trade.
breaks: If you can finish the trade with one ability and leave at once, wave size matters less.

when: you have Ignite and the enemy top has Teleport
asks: I took ignite how do I use it
I have ignite he has tp
when do I fight with ignite
ignite versus teleport
say: You have Ignite, so look for the early all-in while it's your edge, or at least shove them in so Teleport gets spent on lane.
more: Ignite is a lane lead you chose at the start. It pays only if it becomes a kill, a forced recall or plates.
Their Teleport wins the map later. Making them burn it just to get back to lane removes it from the first dragon or grub fight.
check: Whether Ignite is up, and whether their jungler is near.
breaks: If the lane stays even with no kill in sight, stop forcing and match their roams by pushing.

when: you have Teleport and the enemy top has Ignite
asks: he has ignite what do I do
he took ignite and I took tp
can I fight into ignite
ignite top lane how do I play
say: They brought Ignite, so don't take all-ins early; play for farm and Teleport plays, or fight only with your jungler there.
more: They need a kill for their choice to pay. Every minute without one, your Teleport becomes the more valuable spell.
Later it lets you recall freely, join fights on the other side, or save a wave they hoped you would lose.
check: Your health before each wave, and whether their Ignite was just used.
breaks: If Ignite was used and they did not get the kill, there is a window to trade back.

when: enemy jungler just took part in a dragon kill or in a kill on your bot laner or support
asks: their jungler's bot can I fight
jungler showed bot
is now a good time to trade
he's bot do I go

more: A confirmed sighting on the far side means no counter-gank behind your trade. It expires about as fast as he can walk back.
If you cannot win the trade anyway, spend the window on vision; a ward placed now covers his return path.
check: How long ago he was seen, and whether their mid is still in lane.
breaks: If it has been a while since he showed, treat him as unseen again.

when: the enemy top has completed an item and you have not

he just bought can I fight
he's back with items

say: They finished an item first, so keep trades short until yours is done, or recall now if you have the gold for it.
more: Gold counts once it becomes a finished item, and theirs just did. Fights you won two minutes ago can lose now.
The gap closes when you buy. Until then the wave near your tower is where you want to be.
check: How far you are from your own item.
breaks: If you are a level or more ahead, the item matters less and you can still trade evenly.

when: after 4:00 and you are at least one level above the enemy top
asks: I'm a level up should I fight
I out-level him
can I fight him I'm higher level
level lead what do I do
say: You're a level up, which beats a small farm lead, so take the trade now, or use it to zone them off the wave.
more: A level is extra stats and sometimes a stronger ability rank. In early fights it usually matters more than a few minions of gold.
Zoning keeps the gap open: every minion they miss is experience that keeps them a level behind.
check: Whether they just finished an item, which can cancel the level.
breaks: If their jungler is unseen and the wave is on their side, zone from a safe spot rather than chase.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when do I fight as Darius
Darius trading
should I pull him
say: Keep the fight going until Hemorrhage hits five stacks for the big damage, or land the outer edge of Decimate and walk away.
more: Each attack and ability adds a Hemorrhage stack, and at five you gain a large amount of attack damage. Long trades are where you win.
The blade edge of Decimate heals you and hurts more than the handle, so a single clean edge hit is a good short trade on its own.
check: Whether their escape is available; hold Apprehend to pull them back after they use it.
breaks: If they are ranged or can leave freely, do not walk at them; wait for Apprehend range.

asks: how do I trade as Renekton
when do I go in as Renekton

should I use fury
say: Go in when you're above fifty Fury so the ability's empowered, then dash out, or build Fury on minions first if you're low.
more: Fury empowers your abilities, and Cull the Meek heals and hits harder above fifty. A trade without Fury is half a trade.
Slice and Dice is your dash. Use it to reach them, stun with Ruthless Predator, spin, and be gone before their answer.
check: Your Fury bar, and whether you still have a dash to leave with.
breaks: If the dash is spent and their jungler arrives, you have no exit; trade nearer your own side.

asks: how do I trade as Jax
when do I use counter strike
Jax trading
when do I jump on him
say: Leap in with Counter Strike running when they rely on basic attacks, or hold it to turn their jungler's gank.
more: Counter Strike dodges incoming attacks and then stuns everyone around you. Against attack-based champions that is a trade they cannot answer.
Your attack speed climbs with consecutive attacks, so the stun also buys the hits that get it going.
check: Whether their damage is basic attacks or abilities; it does not dodge abilities.
breaks: If you leap in without it and they turn, there is no second escape; use Leap Strike on a minion or ward to leave.

asks: how do I trade as Fiora
when do I riposte
Fiora trading
how do I win trades with vitals
say: Hit the Vital and walk out, since it heals and speeds you up, or hold Riposte for their stun and turn the fight on it.
more: Each Vital hit restores health and gives move speed, so short pokes add up without a real fight.
Riposte parries damage and disables. If it blocks an immobilizing effect it stuns them instead of only slowing, which often decides the trade.
check: Which side the Vital is on, and whether their disable is ready.
breaks: If Riposte is used and missed, back off until it returns; without it you lose to most stuns.

asks: how do I trade as Gnar
when do I fight as Gnar
Gnar rage what do I do
mini or mega
say: Poke and kite as small Gnar, then take the real fight when Rage fills and you turn Mega, or just shove if nobody's in reach.
more: Small Gnar is ranged and quick. Mega Gnar is tougher and brings the crowd control. The lane is about lining up the big form with the fight.
Once you are Mega, a wall behind them turns your ultimate into a stun, so pick the fight near terrain.
check: Your Rage bar, and whether they are standing near terrain.
breaks: If you turned Mega with no fight on offer, use the form to shove the wave rather than chase.

asks: how do I trade as Garen
when do I go in as Garen
Garen trading
do I just run at him
say: Run in with Decisive Strike to silence, spin, then walk out and let Perseverance heal you, or farm if they out-range you.
more: Decisive Strike breaks slows and silences, so they cannot answer during the spin. Leave when it ends.
Perseverance regenerates your health when you have not been hit for a while. You can repeat the trade; most opponents cannot.
check: Whether they can keep hitting you from range, which stops your regeneration.
breaks: If they kite the spin every time, stop trading and outlast them on health.

asks: how do I trade as Teemo
when do I blind

he jumps on me as Teemo
say: Use Blinding Dart as they commit so their attacks are wasted, then keep hitting, or run with Move Quick if help is coming for them.
more: Toxic Shot poisons with every attack, so many small hits win the lane. Blinding Dart is what makes their all-in fail.
Used as poke, the blind is gone when they jump on you. Against attack-based champions keep it for the moment they go in.
check: Whether their gap closer is up, and how far you are from your tower.
breaks: If they fight mostly with abilities, the blind does little; keep your distance instead.

asks: how do I trade as Sett
when do I use haymaker

how do I use grit
say: Take their damage first, then Haymaker for the shield and centre hit, or pull with Facebreaker and keep it short.
more: Haymaker turns the damage you have taken into a shield and a punch that deals true damage in the centre. It is strongest after you have been hit.
Knuckle Down gives speed toward them and two heavier punches, which is the short trade when Haymaker is not charged.
check: How much Grit you have stored, and whether they can step out of the centre line.
breaks: If Haymaker misses, you have no shield and less health; disengage instead of finishing the fight.

when should I back
is it time to base

what about my wave when I ult
say: Shove your wave before you use Stand United so less is lost while you're gone, or hold the ult if that fight's already lost.
more: Stand United shields an ally and then takes you to them, which leaves your lane empty. A wave already at their tower is the cheapest time to go.
Teleport back afterwards if you have it. Otherwise expect to lose a wave and weigh that against what the ult saved.
check: Where your wave is, and whether the fight you would join can still be won.
breaks: If the ally will be dead before you land, don't go; you lose the wave and arrive alone.

Riven trading
how do I use my shield
say: Trade with Broken Wings and Ki Burst, then Valor away so it blocks their answer, or keep Valor if their jungler's unseen.
more: Your abilities charge Runic Blade and each basic attack spends a charge for extra damage. Attack between abilities or you leave damage out.
Valor is a short step that blocks damage. It is both the end of your trade and your only quick way out.
check: Whether their crowd control is ready, and how many of your abilities are up.
breaks: Your abilities all go down together; if the trade didn't win, stay back until they return.

Illaoi trading
when do I use E
say: Fight next to your Tentacles and land Test of Spirit first, or just farm with Tentacle Smash if they won't walk into them.
more: Tentacles grow on nearby walls and swing at spirits and at whoever you hit with Harsh Lesson. Away from them you do far less.
At six, Leap of Faith spawns a Tentacle for each enemy champion hit, so a gank on you can turn if you catch both.
check: Where your Tentacles are, and whether they have a dash to dodge Test of Spirit.
breaks: If Test of Spirit misses, back off; without the spirit you need them to stand still.

Tryndamere trading
when do I ult
say: Build Fury on minions before you trade, since it raises your crit chance, or spin out and heal with Bloodlust if it goes badly.
more: Fury comes from attacks, crits and kills and raises critical strike chance. A full bar makes the same trade far better than an empty one.
At six, Undying Rage means you cannot die while it runs. Use it late, when you are very low and your attack damage is highest.
check: Your Fury bar, and whether Spinning Slash is ready to leave with.
breaks: If they can stun or slow you through the ultimate, diving with it gets you killed when it ends; fight nearer your side.
